English Bluff is the bluff on the west shore of Tsawwassen in the City of Delta, along English Bluff Road above the Strait of Georgia.
Fred Gingell Park at 253 English Bluff Road is the named park on the bluff, listed by the City with picnic tables, trails and a viewpoint.
Tsawwassen Heights and Pebble Hill sit inland and uphill to the east, and Beach Grove is the next shore pocket north along the water.

The confirmed stock is freehold detached houses under the RS zones of Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 along English Bluff Road and its side streets, including bluff-top and waterfront lots on the Strait of Georgia shore.

blocks.text: English Bluff: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Development Permit Area SD2, English Bluff (Tsawwassen Escarpment), is the defining rule on this shore: the Official Community Plan (OCP) Bylaw No. 8400 states the waterfront area is subject to mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, and the ocean-frontage slopes require protection of existing vegetation and tree cover.

SD2 building rules include a Flood Construction Level for habitable floors, no building within 7.5 metres of the natural boundary of the sea or within 7.5 metres of the inboard toe of any dike, and a restrictive covenant on title acknowledging the land may be subject to flooding.

The City's Form S2 guide for sloped lands states a development permit is required for subdivision in SD2, for soil removal or deposit over 2 cubic metres per year on or within 5 metres of the crest of the slope, and for swimming pools unless set back at least 10 metres or two-thirds of the slope height, whichever is greater, from the crest.

A Delta building official can require a geotechnical study wherever, in the official's opinion, land is or is likely to be subject to erosion, land slip, rock falls or avalanche, whether or not a development permit is required.
Delta's small-scale multi-unit housing zoning allows up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots city-wide, but on this shore the SD2 hazard conditions sit on top of that permission.

blocks.text: English Bluff: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Irrigation is a slope issue here, not just a garden choice: the City's sloped-lands guide discourages irrigation systems because leaks can affect slope stability, although systems applying moderate amounts of water do not require a development permit.

Cutting up to two trees can be done without a sloped-lands development permit only if at least 0.6 metres of stump remains standing and the root structure stays intact — and tree cutting is still subject to the Tree Cutting Regulation Bylaw.
Surface water runoff must not be discharged over the crest of the slope for a driveway or path to stay exempt from a development permit under the City's guide.
Emergency slope or flood work does not need a permit first, but the emergency must be reported to the City's Director of Engineering within 48 hours.
South Delta Recreation Centre at 1720 56 Street and the Tsawwassen Library at 1321A 56 Street are the recreation and library services for this shore, both inland in the town centre.

The area-specific cost here is engineering: development in SD2 is subject to conditions set by a suitably qualified Professional Engineer, and a geotechnical study for work in the permit area must be signed and sealed by a Qualified Professional — both are owner-side costs to price into a renovation or rebuild plan.
Route 604 runs English Bluff Road to Bridgeport Station on the Canada Line, and route 620 is the express from the Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal area toward Bridgeport Station.
The BC Ferries Tsawwassen terminal is at the southwest end of Highway 17, with sailings to Swartz Bay, Duke Point, Departure Bay and the Southern Gulf Islands.
English Bluff Road, 12 Avenue, 1 Avenue and 56 Street connect the bluff to Highway 17, Highway 17A and Highway 99.

blocks.text: English Bluff: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check SD2 status for the exact parcel on DeltaMap before offering: the permit area, the Flood Construction Level and the 7.5 metre setbacks are parcel questions, and the City's guide does not certify any individual lot.
Check the title for the SD2 restrictive covenant acknowledging flood risk, and check any existing geotechnical covenant or report registered against the lot.

faq.q: Does the bluff erosion issue affect my lot, or only the waterfront row?
faq.a: Read the permit area, not the street name. SD2 covers the Tsawwassen Escarpment lands the OCP designates for hazardous conditions, and the City's guide triggers a development permit for works near the crest of the slope, including soil movement within 5 metres of the crest and pools close to it. A lot away from the crest can still need a permit, so check the parcel on DeltaMap and ask the City before designing.

faq.q: Which schools serve an English Bluff address?
faq.a: The recorded School District No. Catchments are address-based and SD37 publishes Tsawwassen Area catchment maps, so run the specific address rather than relying on the sample.

faq.q: How do I get to the beach from the bluff?
faq.a: At Fred Gingell Park, 253 English Bluff Road. The City lists the park with trails and a viewpoint, and a City report states stairs at Fred Gingell Park run from the upper park down to the beach. Diefenbaker Park at 5579 1 Avenue, with picnic tables, playgrounds, trails, a viewpoint, washrooms and a water park, is the other named park on this shore.

faq.q: Who owns the beach below a bluff house?
faq.a: The foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land, and Delta states foreshore and water use is interjurisdictional — federal, provincial and City rules all apply. Upland ownership does not include the beach below the natural boundary, and stairs or docks need their tenure checked before a seller markets them as private.

faq.q: Does the bluff affect building or renovating?
faq.a: Yes. Development Permit Area SD2 English Bluff (Tsawwassen Escarpment), Category "b" in OCP Bylaw No. 8400, addresses mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, and development affected by hazardous conditions is subject to conditions set by a suitably qualified Professional Engineer.

faq.q: Where are the parks and beach access?
faq.a: Fred Gingell Park, 253 English Bluff Rd, has stairs from the upper park down to the beach, and Diefenbaker Park, 5579 1 Ave, is the other named park serving this shore.

faq.q: Can a lot add a suite or coach house?
faq.a: Delta's Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing zoning allows up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots, subject to the bylaw and to any slope or streamside permit area on the lot — on this shore, the SD2 hazard conditions are the deciding layer.
